safi-cedvel:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
(the hamza) is for interrogation. (بالدين) is attached to (يكذّب). (the fāʾ) is the connecting fāʾ of the apodosis of an implied condition. (الذي) is a relative in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ذلك). (لا) is negative. (على طعام) is attached to (يحضّ)..
Clause: «رأيت ... » has no grammatical position; it is inceptive.
And the clause: «يكذّب ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
And the clause: «ذلك الذي ... » is in the position of jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if you ask about him, then that is the one who ...
And the clause: «يدعّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative (الذي).
And the clause: «لا يحضّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يدعّ.

safi-cedvel:4-7.t:
* I'rab:
(the fāʾ) is resumptive. (ويل) is a nominative mubtadaʾ. (للمصلين) is attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ ويل. (الذين) is a relative in the position of genitive, a naʿt of المصلين – or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هم" –. (عن صلاتهم) is attached to (ساهون). The second (الذين) is like the first – or it follows the first as a badal –..
Clause: «ويل للمصلّين ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «هم ... ساهون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And the clause: «هم يراءون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
And the clause: «يراءون» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
And the clause: «يمنعون ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يراءون.

* Morphology:
(7) الماعون: a name for the need, of things one benefits from in the house, whether trivial or valuable. It was said that its wazn is فاعول from المعن, which is the small thing – said by Quṭrub – or that it is on the wazn مفعول, by transposition; the original is a passive participle from عان يعون, and it should properly be معون, the original being معوون; then the ʿayn of the word was moved before its fāʾ, giving موعون; then the wāw was changed to alif because of the fatḥa before it: ماعون.

* Benefits:
- Urging on the māʿūn:
The scholars differed about the māʿūn. It is reported from ʿAlī that it is zakāt. Ibn Masʿūd said: the māʿūn is the axe, the bucket and the pot. Mujāhid said: the māʿūn is lending (ʿāriyya). ʿIkrima said: the māʿūn, at its highest, is the obligatory zakāt, and at its lowest, lending of goods. Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurẓī said: the māʿūn is all kindness that people exchange among themselves. The meaning of the verse: it is a prohibition of stinginess and a rebuke against it.
The scholars said: it is recommended for a man to keep in his house a good deal of what the neighbours need, so that he lends it to them and shows them kindness, and he may obtain the reward. [Translator's note: the source reads "ويجوز الثواب" (literally "and the reward is permitted"); translated as written, though "ويحوز" (obtains) may be intended.]
